equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It retains both amplitude and phase
and is a component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field).

The parallel component is defined by

$$
E_{\parallel}=\mathbf{E}_{w}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}_{0}}{|\mathbf{B}_{0}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}_{w}$ is the complex wave-electric-field phasor,
$\mathbf{B}_{0}$ is the local equilibrium magnetic field, and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit direction. The phasor carries the phase of
the harmonic field under the selected time convention.

This quantity is the complex component rather than its magnitude. Its
modulus gives the parallel wave electric field amplitude, while its
quadratures include the [parallel wave electric field imaginary
part](name:parallel_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part) and the
corresponding real part.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field component is directed
along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius
items.description:
Geometric equilibrium coefficient representing a squared flux-coordinate
gradient scaled by the inverse square of major radius.
items.documentation:
This quantity is a geometric metric coefficient for nested magnetic flux
surfaces in toroidal plasma equilibrium. It measures spatial variation of a
flux coordinate after scaling by the inverse square of the major radius,
rather than representing a material, particle, or transport quantity.

For the gradient-ratio form represented by this family, the coefficient is
defined by:

$$
\mathcal{G}(\xi,R) = \frac{|\nabla \xi|^2}{R^2}
$$

where $\mathcal{G}$ is the geometric coefficient, $\xi$ is the relevant
flux-coordinate label, $\nabla \xi$ is its spatial gradient, $|\nabla \xi|$
is the gradient magnitude, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The scope is equilibrium magnetic geometry associated with nested flux
surfaces; no plasma population is selected, and the quantity is not a
density, magnetic-field strength, or transport coefficient. It is the
metric-ratio component of
[square_of_major_radius](name:square_of_major_radius), distinguished from a
bare reciprocal-square-radius factor by the flux-coordinate gradient in its
numerator. The parent quantity is not intrinsically flux-surface averaged;
averaging is an explicit aggregation applied by a child.

The representative [flux-surface-averaged gradient-ratio
coefficient](name:flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius)
is the flux-surface average of this geometric ratio. This distinguishes it
from
[flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_major_radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_major_radius),
which contains the reciprocal-square major-radius factor without the
flux-coordinate gradient factor.

items.name: radial_coordinate_at_inboard_midplane
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of a magnetic flux surface at its inboard midplane
intersection, locating the high-field-side point relative to the toroidal
symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the major-radius coordinate of the point where a magnetic
flux surface intersects the inboard midplane, identifying the
high-field-side location of that surface relative to the toroidal symmetry
axis. It is a locus-specific form of the [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate).

For a magnetic flux surface $\mathcal{S}$, the inboard-midplane radial
coordinate is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{in}}(\mathcal{S}) = R\!\left(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{in}}(\mathcal{S})\right)
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{in}}(\mathcal{S})$ is the quantity defined here,
$R(\mathbf{x})$ is the major-radius coordinate of spatial position
$\mathbf{x}$, $\mathcal{S}$ is the specified magnetic flux surface, and
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{in}}(\mathcal{S})$ is its inboard midplane
intersection. The coordinates are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The scope is one coordinate value for each specified magnetic flux surface
at its inboard, high-field-side midplane intersection. It is not a
flux-surface average, a poloidal or toroidal average, or the corresponding
outboard-midplane coordinate; the latter is represented by [radial
coordinate at outboard
midplane](name:radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane). Unlike [radial
magnetic field](name:radial_magnetic_field), this quantity describes the
location of a surface and not a magnetic-field component.

This quantity specializes [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) by
fixing the evaluation locus to the inboard midplane. Comparing it with the
outboard-midplane value characterizes the horizontal extent and radial
placement of the same magnetic flux surface.

items.name: absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Net electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly from coherent waves to a
selected plasma particle population, integrated over the plasma volume and
resolved by species or charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves
transfer energy directly to selected plasma particles. The selected
population may be electrons, ions, or a specified ion charge state, with the
result integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the
energy of the selected particle population, and the subscript “waves”
restricts the energy-transfer rate to direct coupling from the
electromagnetic wave field. This is the absorbed component of [wave
power](name:wave_power), distinct from electromagnetic power that remains
carried by the wave.

The quantity includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes
subsequent collisional redistribution between particle populations.
Species-resolved and charge-state-resolved instances include [electron
absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) and ion charge-state
absorbed wave power.

items.name: thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power_density
items.description:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into a selected thermal
ion species, summed over all charge states and evaluated locally or as a
flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Thermal-ion absorbed wave power density is the rate at which coherent
electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to the thermal population of
a selected ion species per unit physical volume. It encompasses the local
deposition density and its average over a magnetic flux surface.

The flux-surface-averaged quantity is defined by

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{th},i}
= \left\langle p_{\mathrm{th},i}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
= \left\langle \sum_z \frac{dP_{\mathrm{th},i,z}}{dV}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the local thermal-ion absorbed wave power
density, $\overline{p}_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is its flux-surface average, $i$
identifies the selected ion species, $z$ identifies an ionic charge state,
$P_{\mathrm{th},i,z}$ is the wave power deposited into that species' thermal
population in charge state $z$, $V$ is physical volume, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

The recipient population is the thermal, Maxwellian component of the
selected species, summed over all charge states; no sum over different ion
species is implied. It excludes [fast-ion wave
absorption](name:fast_ion_power_density), electron wave absorption, and
subsequent collisional redistribution of absorbed energy. It is therefore
distinct from a net ion-energy source that combines wave heating with other
source and loss processes.

Summing the flux-surface-averaged contributions from all recipient
populations gives the [flux-surface-averaged total absorbed wave power
density](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_absorbed_wave_power_density).
Integrating this species' local deposition density over the plasma volume
gives its thermal-ion contribution to [absorbed wave
power](name:absorbed_wave_power), rather than another volumetric quantity.

items.name: deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous rate of deuterium particles supplied by active injection,
expressed on a common equivalent-electron basis.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection
systems for deuterium, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. Because
each deuterium atom has nuclear charge number one, the equivalent-electron
rate equals the deuterium particle rate.

The defining relation is

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{D}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)=\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the injected deuterium particle rate, and
$Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the dimensionless deuterium nuclear charge number.
This is a component of the multi-species [source rate due to
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection) and is distinct from the
charge-weighted [electron source rate due to
injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection). It represents
injected inventory supply, not a local volumetric particle source or a net
plasma production-minus-loss rate.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pellet_path
items.description:
Normalized toroidal magnetic-flux surface label assigned to each pellet
location, identifying the nested magnetic surface reached along the pellet’s
in-plasma ablation trajectory.
items.documentation:
This quantity identifies the nested magnetic surface containing the pellet
at a specified location along its in-plasma ablation trajectory. It is a
magnetic-surface coordinate, not a cylindrical distance or a local vector
component.

At pellet position $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}$, the normalized toroidal flux
coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}) = \left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right]^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate,
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p}$ is the pellet position,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm p})$ is the toroidal magnetic flux
labeling the magnetic surface through that position,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its value at the equilibrium boundary. The
position is interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The scope is the pellet’s in-plasma ablation trajectory, with the coordinate
evaluated pointwise at each pellet location. It does not represent distance
traveled along the path, a path integral, an average over the trajectory, or
an aggregate over multiple pellets.

This is the locus-specific realization of the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). The axis and boundary
references set the coordinate endpoints, so the value increases outward
across nested magnetic surfaces while remaining distinct from a cylindrical
radial coordinate.

items.name: pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Thermal pressure of a plasma constituent or neutral-gas population in the
open-field-line scrape-off layer, the region between the last closed flux
surface and the material plasma-facing components.
items.documentation:
The scrape-off layer (SOL) is the open-field-line region extending from the
last closed flux surface to the material plasma-facing components, where
local pressure governs energy and particle exhaust, neutral recycling,
ionization balance, and the onset of divertor detachment. This parent name
generalizes over species-resolved SOL pressure quantities: [electron
pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) represents the electron
partial pressure and additionally anchors the pressure baseline offset in
H-mode pedestal profile fits, while [neutral pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) characterizes the
neutral gas inventory affecting recycling, pumping balance, and detachment
control.

For any thermally equilibrated species $s$, the scalar thermal pressure
satisfies:

$$
p_s = n_s k_B T_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the species number density and $T_s$ is its temperature in
energy units.

SOL pressure is inferred from a combination of diagnostics: Langmuir probes
provide local electron pressure at plasma-facing surfaces from saturation
current and electron temperature; neutral gas pressure gages directly
measure gas pressure in the divertor pumping region; Thomson scattering
resolves electron density and temperature profiles from which electron
pressure is derived. The characteristic radial scale over which pressure
falls from the separatrix outward is described by the [decay length over the
scrape-off layer](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

items.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity
items.description:
Fickian coefficient relating density-normalized diffusive thermal-energy
flux of neutrals in one species and internal state to their temperature
gradient along the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral internal-state energy diffusivity quantifies
gradient-driven transport of thermal energy carried by a specified neutral
species in one internal state, along the local magnetic-field direction. The
magnetic field defines the projection direction; it does not imply that
neutral particles are magnetically confined.

The density-normalized diffusive thermal-energy flux satisfies:

$$
\frac{Q_{0,a,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{0,a}} = -D_{0,a,W,\parallel}\,\mathbf{b}\cdot\nabla(k_B T_{0,a})
$$

where $D_{0,a,W,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity,
$Q_{0,a,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the field-parallel projection of the
diffusive thermal-energy flux, $n_{0,a}$ is the population's number density,
and $T_{0,a}$ is its thermodynamic temperature. The symbol $k_B$ is
Boltzmann's constant, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. The
subscripts $0$, $a$, and $W$ identify neutral particles, the specified
internal state, and the energy transport channel, respectively. The minus
sign denotes transport down the temperature gradient for a nonnegative
diffusivity.

This coefficient applies to one neutral species and internal state; it is
neither summed nor averaged over species or internal states. It describes
only the field-aligned diffusive contribution, excluding convective and
advective energy transport and transport perpendicular to the magnetic
field.

The [poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity)
describes the corresponding state-resolved transport coefficient in the
poloidal direction, which is distinct from the local magnetic-field
direction.

items.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon ions at the
magnetic axis, averaged over all neon ionization states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the neon impurity-ion bulk
velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the density-weighted mean
over all neon ionization states and excludes neutral neon.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined
by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}}=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the charge-state-aggregated neon-ion
bulk velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle. The magnetic axis is the point
inside the confined plasma where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux
$\psi$ vanishes, $\nabla\psi=0$. The analogous quantity at the plasma
boundary is [toroidal neon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the neon-ion bulk flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_angular_width_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Full toroidal angular width of the spectrometer-channel spatial-resolution
region in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, including effective
spatial-resolution broadening. The toroidal angle φ increases
counterclockwise when viewed from above +Z.
items.documentation:
Full toroidal angular width of a spectrometer-channel spatial-resolution
region is the non-negative span in toroidal angle covered by the region
associated with that channel, including its effective spatial-resolution
broadening. The toroidal angle $\phi$ is the angular coordinate in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$Z$ is vertical height, and $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed
from the $+\hat{Z}$ side.

For a channel $c$ with spatial-resolution region $\Omega_c$, the width is

$$
\Delta\phi_c = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in\Omega_c} \tilde{\phi}(\mathbf{x}) - \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\Omega_c} \tilde{\phi}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\Delta\phi_c$ is the toroidal angular width, $\Omega_c$ is the
spatial-resolution region of channel $c$, and $\tilde{\phi}(\mathbf{x})$ is
a continuously unwrapped toroidal angle of point $\mathbf{x}$ over that
region.

It is an angular extent, not a center coordinate, orientation, or signed
toroidal displacement. If the region crosses a toroidal-angle branch cut,
the unwrapped angle is chosen so the expression gives the full physical span
of the region; this width may be used as a geometric factor in viewing
étendue, but it is not an étendue.

items.name: ion_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity coefficient for diamagnetic, advective, non-diffusive
transport of aggregate ion momentum, distinct from the ions’ actual bulk
flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the diamagnetic
contribution to advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum for the ion
population, selected momentum component, and transport direction. It is a
transport-closure quantity rather than the actual bulk flow velocity of the
ions.

For the selected momentum component and transport direction, the diamagnetic
convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}} = V_{\mathrm{ion,dia}} P_{\mathrm{ion}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to
convective ion-momentum flux, $V_{\mathrm{ion,dia}}$ is this effective
convection velocity, $P_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the corresponding ion momentum
density, and the subscript $\mathrm{dia}$ identifies the diamagnetic
contribution.

The quantity applies to the aggregate ion population and uses the
density-weighted mean over all ion charge states, rather than resolving one
particular charge state. It represents only the diamagnetic advective
contribution; neutral-particle transport, diffusive momentum transport, and
the ions’ actual bulk flow velocity are excluded.

This is the ion-population specialization of the [diamagnetic momentum
convection velocity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity). The
[ion charge-state diamagnetic momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity)
resolves the corresponding effective coefficient for one ion charge state
instead of the charge-state-aggregated ion population.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated diamagnetic momentum flux is
outward, toward the last closed flux surface, for positive transported ion
momentum density.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_source
items.description:
Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single
resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral
population. It includes charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and
elastic collisions.
items.documentation:
Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single
resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral
population after normalization by the transport area. It represents the
vector rate at which charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic
collisions add momentum to, or remove momentum from, that resolved neutral
state.

The defining process decomposition is:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)} = \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cx}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{ion}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{rec}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{el}}
$$

where \(\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)}\) is this momentum source for neutral
species \(n\) in internal state \(\alpha\), and the terms on the right are
the contributions from charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and
elastic collisions, respectively.

The quantity is resolved for one neutral species and one internal state; it
is not the state-summed [neutral momentum
source](name:neutral_momentum_source), which is obtained by summing this
vector over all resolved internal states of that neutral species. It is the
neutral-state analog of the [ion charge-state momentum
source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), with resolution by internal
state rather than ion charge state. A directional component such as the
[radial neutral-internal-state momentum
source](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) is the
projection of this vector onto the corresponding direction; `radial` denotes
the \(\hat{R}\) component in the right-handed cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\)
frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})\).

Sign convention: Positive when a vector component represents momentum
transferred to the neutral species in the resolved internal state along the
positive basis direction used for that component; in the right-handed
cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\) frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi},
\hat{Z})\), the radial, toroidal, and vertical components are positive along
\(+\hat{R}\), increasing toroidal angle \(\phi\), and \(+\hat{Z}\),
respectively.

items.name: thermal_ion_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress from random motion,
summed over ionic charge states and excluding fast-ion and bulk-flow
contributions.
items.documentation:
Pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress arising from random
motion about each thermal population's mean flow. It is the thermal
contribution to [ion pressure](name:ion_pressure), rather than the combined
thermal and nonthermal ion pressure.

The thermal pressure is defined by the central second velocity moment:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{1}{3}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}_i}\sum_c m_s\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c}|^2 f^{\mathrm{th}}_{s,c}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal ion pressure, $\mathcal{S}_i$ is
the selected set of ion species, $s$ labels species, $c$ labels ionic charge
state, $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ is the mean velocity of the corresponding thermal
population, $f^{\mathrm{th}}_{s,c}$ is its local velocity distribution
function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

For a species-resolved quantity, the species set contains only that species.
All ionic charge states are included through a direct additive sum of their
[thermal pressures](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure), not a
density-weighted mean. Fast-ion pressure, electron pressure, and kinetic
stress associated with directed bulk motion are excluded. The quantity is
isotropic pressure, not a separately selected field-parallel or
field-perpendicular stress component.

Summing the species-resolved contributions over every ion species gives
[total thermal ion pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure). That total is
the ion contribution to [thermal plasma
pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure), which additionally includes
thermal-electron pressure.

items.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection
items.description:
Power deposited on a single divertor target by convective plasma particle
flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by
streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
Convective power at a single divertor target quantifies the energy
transported to that target by plasma particles streaming from the scrape-off
layer. It includes thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried into
the material surface and is the target-local contribution to [power due to
convection](name:power_due_to_convection).

The target-integrated convective power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{conv,target}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{target}}} \sum_s n_s v_{n,s} \left[ \frac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_s-1} k_B T_s + \frac{1}{2}m_s v_{n,s}^{2} \right] \, dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the wetted target surface, $n_s$ is the
number density of species $s$, $v_{n,s}$ is its flow speed normal to and
into the target, $\gamma_s$ is its adiabatic index, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's
constant, $T_s$ is its temperature, and $m_s$ is its particle mass. The
species sum includes the particle channels assigned to convective transport
and excludes conductive and radiative deposition.

This quantity applies to one target; summing corresponding target
contributions gives [convective power of the
divertor](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection).

items.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density
items.description:
Toroidal current density carried by co-passing fast particles, averaged over
a magnetic flux surface and excluding compensating electron and thermal-ion
return currents.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density carried by co-passing fast particles is the
flux-surface-averaged toroidal projection of [co-passing fast-particle
current density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density). The particles are
nonthermal and follow untrapped guiding-center orbits whose toroidal transit
is in the plasma-current direction.

The averaged projection is defined by:

$$
j_\phi = \left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co,fast}}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right\rangle
$$

where $j_\phi$ is this toroidal current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the co-passing fast-particle
current-density vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector
toward increasing toroidal angle. The brackets denote a volume-weighted
average over an infinitesimal shell between neighboring magnetic flux
surfaces. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the co-passing portion of the fast-particle distribution contributes.
Multiple distributions representing the same fast-particle species are
superposed. Compensating electron and thermal-ion drag currents are
excluded, so this quantity is not the net driven current density including
those return currents.

This is one signed component contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), not the magnitude of its vector parent. The
[toroidal counter-passing fast-particle current
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density) and [toroidal
trapped fast-particle current
density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density) describe separate
orbit-class contributions and are not included here. Co-passing
classification is relative to the plasma-current direction and does not
itself imply a positive toroidal component.

Sign convention: Positive when the surface-averaged conventional
fast-particle charge flux is directed toward increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: maximum_surface_temperature
items.description:
Peak apparent temperature of the exposed plasma-facing surface over all
valid points within a defined infrared-camera region of interest.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the largest apparent temperature assigned to the exposed
material surface of a plasma-facing component within a specified
infrared-camera region of interest. It is an extremum of the local [surface
temperature](name:surface_temperature), not a local value, area average, or
heat-flux measure.

$$
T_{\mathrm{max,ROI}} = \max_{\mathbf{x} \in V_{\mathrm{ROI}}} T_s(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $T_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the surface temperature at surface position
$\mathbf{x}$, and $V_{\mathrm{ROI}}$ is the set of valid surface positions
in the defined region of interest. Points excluded from the valid set do not
contribute to the maximum.

items.name: electron_temperature_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Kinetic temperature of the electron population evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
Kinetic temperature at an internal transport barrier is the
energy-equivalent measure of random motion for the electron population on
the barrier’s assigned flux surface. It is the electron-specific member of
the temperature family.

For an isotropic electron population, the defining relation is:

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_e\rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron kinetic temperature and $\langle E_e\rangle$ is
the mean random kinetic energy per electron. The quantity applies only to
electrons and is distinct from the ion-population average temperature at an
internal transport barrier. It is a local value on the assigned core flux
surface, not an integral across the barrier; the population-unspecified
parent is temperature at an internal transport barrier.

items.name: ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count
items.description:
Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ND3
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count with 10 count units per molecule.
items.documentation:
Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterated
ammonia (ND3) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown,
expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ND3 molecule
contributes ten equivalent electrons: seven from nitrogen and one from each
of its three deuterium atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = 10\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are atomic numbers,
$N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated molecule count,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}$ is the molecule injection rate, and $t_0$ and
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times.

This quantity includes only ND3 introduced before breakdown and excludes
wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and
retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterated-ammonia component of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count), distinct from
[ammonia_prefill_count](name:ammonia_prefill_count) and post-breakdown
[accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count).

items.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density
items.description:
Mean number density of runaway electrons over the confined plasma volume,
obtained by averaging the local suprathermal population that remains in the
accelerating tail.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged runaway electron density is the spatial mean of the local
runaway-electron population over the confined plasma volume. Runaway
electrons are suprathermal electrons whose momentum makes collisional
slowing-down ineffective compared with continued electromagnetic
acceleration, as described by
[runaway_electron_density](name:runaway_electron_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE}$ is the volume-averaged runaway electron
density, $n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local runaway electron density
at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, and
$\mathrm{d}V$ is the physical volume element.

This quantity averages the local density rather than reporting the total
runaway-electron count; the latter is obtained by multiplying the average by
$V_\mathrm{p}$. It includes the full confined plasma volume and excludes
regions outside that volume.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity
items.description:
Signed mean ion flow along the poloidal tangent for one specified species
and ionization charge state, distinct from thermal motion and
charge-state-averaged flow.
items.documentation:
The poloidal ion charge-state velocity is the local poloidal projection of
the bulk-flow velocity of ions belonging to one specified species and
ionization charge state. It describes directed motion after averaging over
particle velocities, rather than the random thermal velocity spread.

For a nonzero charge-state population, the component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{p},q}=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\mathbf u_q=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\frac{\int\mathbf v f_q(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_q(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{\mathrm{p},q}$ is the poloidal velocity component, $q$ identifies
the ionic charge number, $\mathbf u_q$ is the [ion charge-state
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity,
and $f_q$ is the local velocity distribution of the selected species and
charge state. The vector $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the unit poloidal
tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the specified
flux-coordinate frame $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels magnetic
surfaces and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The orientation of $\theta$ must
be specified with that frame.

This quantity retains charge-state resolution and implies neither
charge-state averaging nor flux-surface averaging. No particular spatial
locus is imposed. The [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity), by contrast, is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of the selected species.

Unlike the [parallel ion charge-state
velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity), which projects along the
local magnetic field, this component projects along the poloidal tangent. It
is also distinct from the effective [poloidal ion-state momentum convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_state_momentum_convection_velocity), which
parameterizes momentum transport rather than defining the population's first
velocity moment.

Sign convention: Positive when the bulk flow of the selected ion charge
state projects toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Vertical Z coordinate of the geometric center of a soft X-ray detector in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical Z coordinate of the geometric center of a soft X-ray detector is
the height coordinate of that detector center in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The origin of $Z$ is the machine
midplane, so $Z=0$ lies on that midplane.

Together with the corresponding major-radius and toroidal-angle coordinates,
this quantity specifies the absolute geometric position of the detector
center. It is distinct from a detector-pixel coordinate, an aperture
position, a line-of-sight direction, and any measured soft-X-ray signal.

Sign convention: Positive when the detector center is above the machine
midplane in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of positively charged tungsten ions on
the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all ionization states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the number density of tungsten ions averaged over the last
closed magnetic flux surface, with all positive ionization states included
and neutral tungsten excluded. It is the surface-averaged counterpart of the
local tungsten density at the plasma boundary.

The flux-surface average at the plasma-boundary flux label is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm{W}}\,d\ell_p/B_p}{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} d\ell_p/B_p}
$$

where $\psi_b$ is the flux label of the plasma boundary, $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is
the local summed tungsten-ion density, $d\ell_p$ is poloidal contour length,
and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. The quantity is distinct
from [volume-averaged tungsten
density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), which averages over the
enclosed plasma volume.

items.name: toroidal_diamagnetic_magnetic_flux_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Toroidal diamagnetic magnetic flux at an inside flux surface is the
diamagnetic contribution to the toroidal magnetic flux through the poloidal
cross-section enclosed by a selected closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
Toroidal diamagnetic magnetic flux at an inside flux surface is the
diamagnetic contribution to the [toroidal magnetic
flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux) through the poloidal cross-section
enclosed by a selected closed flux surface. It is a surface-dependent
cumulative flux inside the plasma boundary, not only a boundary value.

For an axisymmetric equilibrium in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing
counter-clockwise viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height,
let $S_\chi$ be the constant-$\phi$ poloidal cross-section enclosed by the
flux surface labeled by $\chi$. With $d\mathbf{A}_\phi = \hat{\phi}\,dA$
oriented toward increasing $\phi$, the enclosed diamagnetic toroidal flux is
defined by:

$$
\Phi_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}}(\chi) = \int_{S_\chi} \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}(R,Z) \cdot d\mathbf{A}_\phi = \int_{S_\chi} B_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $\chi$ identifies the selected flux surface,
$\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to the
equilibrium magnetic field, $B_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}} =
\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is its toroidal component,
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle, and $dA$
is the positive scalar area element on $S_\chi$.

This quantity includes only the diamagnetic magnetic-field contribution. It
is distinct from the total
[toroidal_magnetic_flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux), which includes all
magnetic-field contributions, from
[toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary),
which is evaluated at the plasma boundary, and from
[toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current),
which isolates the poloidal-current contribution at that boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net diamagnetic magnetic-field
contribution through the enclosed poloidal cross-section points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, counter-clockwise viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: derivative_of_poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate
items.description:
Rate at which the poloidal-plane area enclosed by a nested magnetic flux
surface changes with signed poloidal magnetic flux; it supplies a geometric
metric for flux-surface averages.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric derivative of the area enclosed by a nested,
closed magnetic flux surface in a poloidal cross-section. It describes how
neighboring flux surfaces differ in enclosed poloidal-plane area.

$$
\frac{dA}{d\psi}
$$

where $A(\psi)$ is the area enclosed by the flux surface labeled by signed
poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$. The area is measured in the poloidal plane of
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to the cumulative enclosed area of each nested closed
flux surface and is not a local area density, toroidal surface area, or
enclosed-volume derivative. The corresponding [derivative of volume of flux
surface with respect to poloidal magnetic flux
coordinate](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate)
differentiates enclosed volume rather than cross-sectional area, while the
derivative of area of flux surface with respect to toroidal flux coordinate
uses the toroidal magnetic flux coordinate instead of $\psi$.

Sign convention: Positive when the enclosed poloidal-plane area increases in
the direction of increasing signed poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$, with
positive flux oriented by the $+Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: maximum_gas_flow
items.description:
Maximum gas flow is the largest pressure-volume throughput that a gas
injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the upper bound of its
controllable range.
items.documentation:
Maximum gas flow is the upper reliable operating limit of the
pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It represents
the aggregate gas stream rather than a particular molecular species, charge
state, mass flow, or particle-number rate.

The defining pressure-volume throughput at the upper delivery limit is

$$
Q_g^{\max} = p_g \frac{dV_g}{dt}
$$

where $Q_g^{\max}$ is the maximum gas pressure-volume throughput, $p_g$ is
the gas pressure at the flow boundary, $V_g$ is the volume of gas crossing
that boundary, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to gas delivered through a gas injection valve for
fueling, impurity seeding, or disruption mitigation. The maximum qualifier
denotes a reliable upper delivery limit for the aggregate gas stream, not a
species-resolved flow, mass-flow rate, or particle-number rate.

The quantity is the upper-bound member of the gas flow family: gas flow
denotes the same pressure-volume throughput without an upper-limit
restriction, while [minimum gas flow](name:minimum_gas_flow) denotes its
lower reliable operating limit.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_filter_window
items.description:
First local tangential width of the filter window is its full
rectangular-aperture extent along the object-local first tangential axis.
items.documentation:
Width of filter window

For rectangular geometry, the full width is the difference between the
greatest and least boundary coordinates along that axis:

$$
w = \xi_{1,\max} - \xi_{1,\min}
$$

where $w$ is the first local tangential width, and $\xi_{1,\max}$ and
$\xi_{1,\min}$ are the greatest and least values, respectively, of the
[first local tangential coordinate of the filter
window](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_filter_window) on the
aperture boundary.

This quantity applies to one filter window only when its geometry is
rectangular. It is a full width, not a half-width or a signed boundary
coordinate, and is distinct from the [filter-window
radius](name:radius_of_filter_window), which describes the opening for
circular geometry.

Together with the [second local tangential width of the filter
window](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_filter_window), it specifies
the two orthogonal dimensions of the rectangular aperture.

items.name: electron_particle_flux
items.description:
Electron particle flux is the net number of electrons crossing an oriented
surface per unit actual surface area and time, with opposite crossing
directions counted with opposite signs.
items.documentation:
Electron particle flux is the signed net number flow of free electrons
through an oriented surface per unit actual surface area and time. It is the
surface-normal projection of electron number transport, without selecting a
fixed geometric or magnetic-field direction.

The local flux is defined by the normal velocity moment of the electron
distribution:

$$
\Gamma_e = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}) f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_e$ is the electron particle flux, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron
velocity relative to the surface, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen surface
unit normal, $f_e$ is the local electron velocity distribution normalized so
that its velocity integral equals the electron number density, and $d^3v$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity enters the electron number balance and does not select a
particular electron subpopulation, transport mechanism, or plasma region.
Diffusive and convective contributions add to the net particle transport. It
is a local per-area flux, not an area-integrated particle rate or a one-way
incident or emitted flux.

The [radial](name:radial_electron_particle_flux),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_electron_particle_flux), and [parallel electron
particle fluxes](name:parallel_electron_particle_flux) specialize this
definition by choosing the corresponding direction for the surface normal.
Unlike [electron energy flux](name:electron_energy_flux), this quantity
counts electrons rather than weighting their crossings by kinetic energy.

Sign convention: Positive when the net electron flow follows the chosen
surface normal; the negative electric charge of electrons does not reverse
this particle-flux sign.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
items.description:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux is the signed net number flow
of one neutral species in a specified internal quantum state per area
perpendicular to the local poloidal direction.
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux is the local net number
transport of one neutral atomic or molecular species in a specified internal
quantum state along the poloidal direction. It counts oppositely directed
crossings with opposite signs, using area perpendicular to that direction.

The component is the poloidal projection of the state-resolved particle-flux
vector:

$$
\Gamma^{0}_{a,\mathrm p} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p} = \int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}) f^{0}_{a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma^{0}_{a,\mathrm p}$ is this poloidal component,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{a}$ is the neutral particle-flux vector for the
selected species and state, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the local
poloidal unit vector, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, $f^{0}_{a}$ is the
velocity distribution normalized to the state's number density, and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space volume element. The superscript $0$ identifies
neutrals, $a$ labels the internal state, and $\mathrm p$ identifies the
poloidal projection.

The poloidal direction lies in a plane of constant toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position. Its
orientation follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ around the magnetic
axis; the orientation of $\theta$ must be specified independently of the
magnetic-field direction.

This specializes [neutral internal-state particle
flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) to a surface normal aligned
with the poloidal direction. It includes thermal and nonthermal neutrals in
the selected state and is neither a sum over internal states nor a
surface-integrated arrival rate. Summing over all internal states of the
same species gives the [poloidal neutral particle
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux). The [parallel neutral
internal-state particle
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) instead projects
transport along the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when net neutral particle transport is toward
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Neutral-particle power deposited on a divertor target by recombination
processes at the plasma-material interface, excluding the plasma-ion
recombination channel.
items.documentation:
This quantity captures the neutral-particle recombination power delivered to
a single divertor target, encompassing energy deposited when neutral
particles recombine into lower-energy bound states at the plasma-material
interface. Only the fraction of released binding, internal, and kinetic
energy accommodated by the target material contributes to this quantity.

The target-localized neutral recombination power is the inward surface
integral of the neutral-recombination energy-flux vector over the wetted
target area:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rec,n,target}} = \int_{\mathcal{A}_t} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{rec,n}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{mat}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{rec,n,target}}$ is the neutral-particle recombination
power at the target, $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{rec,n}}$ is the energy-flux vector
due only to neutral-particle recombination,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{mat}}$ is the unit normal to the target surface
directed into the material, and $\mathcal{A}_t$ is the target area receiving
that contribution.

This target-localized quantity is the neutral-particle channel of
[power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination),
distinct from
[plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination),
which describes recombination of plasma ions. It excludes conducted,
convected, radiative, charge-exchange, ionization, and plasma-ion
recombination heat loads. Summed over all divertor targets, it gives
[neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).

items.name: thomson_scattering_laser_pulse_energy_at_outlet
items.description:
Energy carried by a Thomson-scattering probing laser pulse after it has
traversed the plasma, representing the transmitted post-plasma pulse.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total energy carried by a Thomson-scattering laser
pulse at the beam exit after crossing the plasma. It represents the
transmitted pulse available for comparison with the pre-plasma pulse.

The pulse energy is defined by the time integral of the outgoing laser
power:

$$
E_{\mathrm{out}} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} P_{\mathrm{out}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the post-plasma laser-pulse energy,
$P_{\mathrm{out}}(t)$ is the laser power exiting the plasma at time $t$, and
$t_1$ and $t_2$ delimit the pulse.

The scope is restricted to the probing laser pulse after plasma crossing and
includes the complete pulse over its temporal extent. It excludes the
incident pre-plasma pulse energy, energy deposited in the plasma, and
Thomson-scattered radiation. The ratio of this quantity to the corresponding
incident pulse energy defines the pulse transmission factor and quantifies
attenuation through the plasma.

items.name: momentum_source_rate
items.description:
Rate characterizing the addition, removal, or transfer of momentum to a
plasma population, expressed relative to its associated momentum content.
items.documentation:
This quantity is a scalar rate for momentum supplied to, removed from, or
transferred within a plasma population. It describes the temporal strength
of a momentum source without selecting a particular particle species,
direction, mechanism, or spatial region.

When the source is expressed relative to the associated momentum density,
its defining relation is

$$
\nu_{p,\mathrm{src}} = \frac{S_p}{P}
$$

where $\nu_{p,\mathrm{src}}$ is the momentum source rate, $S_p$ is the
momentum source density, and $P$ is the corresponding momentum density. The
parent covers concrete specializations such as the [ion momentum source
rate](name:ion_momentum_source_rate), while excluding the momentum density
itself and any directional component not specified by the specialization.

items.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_line_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
items.description:
Dimensionless line-averaged protium fraction among hydrogenic ions, obtained
by dividing the protium density by the total hydrogenic density along the
same chord.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the fraction of hydrogenic ion content carried by protium
along a specified chord through the plasma. It is a ratio of consistently
line-averaged densities, rather than a local fraction or a volume-averaged
fraction.

$$
f_{\rm H}^{\rm line} = \frac{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}}{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}}
$$

where $f_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium fraction,
$\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium-ion number
density, $\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding deuterium-ion
number density, and $\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding
tritium-ion number density. The symbols H, D, and T denote protium,
deuterium, and tritium, respectively.

The quantity applies to the hydrogenic ion population along one common chord
and aggregates the isotope densities through the total hydrogenic
denominator. Neutral atomic hydrogen and non-hydrogenic species are
excluded. The numerator is the [line-averaged hydrogen
density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator is the
[total hydrogenic density](name:total_hydrogenic_density) under the same
line-averaging convention.

This ratio differs from the [ratio of volume-averaged hydrogen density to
volume-averaged total hydrogenic
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density),
because the latter uses volume-averaged rather than chord-averaged isotope
densities.

items.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, photon emission,
and secondary-electron emission. The transported quantity may be particle
number, energy, momentum, or radiative power in a more specific member.
items.documentation:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, thermal
evaporation, photon emission, secondary-electron emission, or surface
de-excitation. It is the surface-normal flux density generated by the
material response at the wall and carried from the material side toward the
plasma side.

The emission flux is related to incident driving fluxes through
surface-emission yield or response coefficients:

$$
F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}} = \sum_k Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}} F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}
$$

where $F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted flux density of physical quantity
$Q$, $F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is incident channel $k$ that drives surface
emission, and $Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the surface-emission coefficient
for producing the emitted $Q$ flux.

This quantity is the wall-specific member of
[flux_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_due_to_surface_emission) and is an
abstraction over component channels. The energy channel is
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
while energy_flux_at_wall denotes energy flux at the wall without specifying
surface emission as the cause. It excludes flux incident on the wall from
the plasma or radiation field except as a driver of emission;
flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation denotes radiative flux at the wall rather than
material emission generated by the wall.

Sign convention: Positive when the net emitted flux is directed from the
wall material into the plasma.

items.name: launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description:
Radio-frequency power launched toward the plasma by an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna, equal to forward incident power minus reflected return power.
items.documentation:
The quantity denotes radio-frequency wave power launched toward the plasma
by an ion-cyclotron resonance heating antenna at the antenna reference
plane. It is the net launched component after accounting for the forward and
reflected traveling-wave components.

For a single antenna, the launched power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{launched}} = P_{\mathrm{fwd}} - P_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the launched radio-frequency power,
$P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the forward incident power traveling from the
generator toward the antenna, and $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reflected power
traveling from the antenna toward the generator.

This quantity applies to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna at its reference
plane and represents a net directional power, not a sum over an antenna set.
It excludes the reflected component and the power subsequently absorbed by
the plasma.

Within the broader power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna quantity, this
is the launched-power specialization. The [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and [reflected
power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) are the
components combined by the defining relation, whereas power due to
ion-cyclotron heating denotes power coupled from the waves into the plasma.

items.name: radial_neutral_particle_flux
items.description:
Radial neutral particle flux is the signed net number flow per unit area and
time toward increasing major radius for one neutral atomic or molecular
species, summed over its internal states. It is the cylindrical major-radius
component, not the flux-surface-normal component.
items.documentation:
Radial neutral particle flux is the signed component of neutral
particle-number transport in the direction of increasing major radius. It
gives the net number flow per area and time for one neutral atomic or
molecular species, with that species’ internal states combined.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, its defining
projection and internal-state aggregation are:

$$
\Gamma_{0,R} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}} = \sum_a \Gamma_{0,a,R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,R}$ is the radial neutral particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is the [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) for one species summed over its internal
states, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major
radius, $a$ indexes the internal states of that species, and
$\Gamma_{0,a,R}$ is its [radial neutral internal-state particle
flux](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux). Here, $R$ is major
radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to one neutral species, includes all its internal
states, and does not sum over distinct neutral species or include charged
particles. It is a flux density, not a surface-integrated particle rate. A
flux-surface-averaged transport value is the average of this radial
component over the surface; the major-radius direction is not generally
normal to a magnetic flux surface, so this average is not the
flux-surface-normal component.

This is the major-radius projection of [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux), and summing the state-resolved radial
contributions gives the species-level quantity. [Poloidal neutral particle
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux) and [parallel neutral particle
flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux) are distinct directional
projections of neutral particle transport. The flux-surface-averaged form
represents radial neutral transport in the neutral particle balance.

Sign convention: Positive when the net neutral particle flux has a component
toward increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: density_at_limiter
items.description:
Local number density of a selected charged plasma population evaluated
immediately on the plasma-facing side of a limiter surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local number density of a selected charged plasma
population at the plasma-facing side of a limiter. The selection may be
electrons, an ion species summed over its ionization states, or a defined
fuel pseudo-species formed by combining constituent ion populations.

$$
n_s(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_s}{dV}
$$

where $n_s$ is the selected population number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_s$ is
the number of counted particles, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$
is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. The position is immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing
limiter, on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

Population aggregation is part of the specialization: ion species quantities
may be summed over positive ionization states while excluding neutrals,
electrons count the electron population, and the deuterium–tritium
pseudo-species combines the corresponding ion densities. Concrete members
include [electron density at a limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter),
ion density at a limiter, and [deuterium-tritium density at a
limiter](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter). The bare quantity does
not imply a sum over all charged populations.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position
items.description:
Vertical Z coordinate of the physical point from which a heating beam or
wave is launched, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate $Z$ of the launching position locates the spatial
origin of a beam or electromagnetic wave's propagation trajectory within the
tokamak vessel, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where
$Z$ is the height along the machine symmetry axis.

For electron cyclotron heating systems, this coordinate specifies the height
at which the EC beam exits the launcher and enters the plasma. Together with
the major-radius and toroidal-angle components, it fully defines the
three-dimensional launch-point geometry needed for beam-tracing and
current-drive modeling. The angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
determines the beam injection direction from this spatial origin, while
[vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_line_of_sight)
gives $Z$ at discrete computed points along the propagating ray rather than
at its origin.

The launch height is set by the mechanical installation of the launcher on
the vacuum vessel and is determined by engineering survey. For
equatorial-port launchers, $Z$ is close to 0 m; upper-port or top-launch
geometries place the origin at $Z \approx 0.5$–$1.5$ m in medium-to-large
tokamaks.

items.name: helium_3_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Helium-3 ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states
and excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
items.documentation:
Helium-3 density at a limiter is the local number density of helium-3 ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_{^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{^3\mathrm{He}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density,
$N_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the counted number of helium-3 ions, $V$ is volume,
and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The density is summed over all positive helium-3 ionization states and
excludes neutral helium-3 atoms. It is the helium-3-specific member of
[density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and differs from ion density
at a limiter, which is not restricted to helium-3; [helium-4 density at a
limiter](name:helium_4_density_at_limiter) describes the corresponding
isotope.

items.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal component of the lithium impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the H-mode pedestal top. It represents the local azimuthal rotation of
lithium impurity ions at the steep-gradient edge transport barrier, not a
pedestal-region average.
items.documentation:
The toroidal lithium ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top is the
$\hat{\phi}$-projection of the lithium impurity ion mean velocity vector at
the radial reference location where the H-mode edge transport barrier
steep-gradient region joins the flatter core profile. This is a
point-evaluated quantity, not a spatial average over the pedestal region.

The toroidal component is defined as:

$$
v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium ion fluid velocity vector
and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Lithium toroidal rotation at the pedestal is inferred from charge exchange
recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) using Doppler shifts of lithium spectral
lines following charge exchange with an injected neutral beam. The
pedestal-top reference location is identified from the steep-gradient region
of the relevant kinetic profile. Comparable pedestal-top rotation
measurements for other impurity species are provided by
[toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top)
and
[toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top);
the lithium ion rotation at other radial reference points is covered by
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis)
and
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when $v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}}$ points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered by Coulomb
collisions to trapped fast ions interacting with a specified ion charge
state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum source density
transferred to the trapped fast-ion population through Coulomb collisions
with a specified ion charge state. It is the toroidal component of the
collisional torque contribution identified by the [trapped fast-ion
charge-state collisional torque
density](name:trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The toroidal torque density is related to the toroidal collisional force
density by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal torque density, $R$ is the
major radius measured from the symmetry axis, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$
is the toroidal component of the collisional force density transferred to
trapped fast ions. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Only the trapped fast-ion contribution and the specified ion-charge-state
collision channel are included; passing-orbit contributions such as
[toroidal counter-passing fast ion charge-state collisional torque
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
are excluded. This quantity is a local density, not a volume-integrated
toroidal torque.

Sign convention: Positive when the collisional force transferred to the
trapped fast-ion population has a toroidal component in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_ohmic_dissipation
items.description:
Power deposited on all divertor targets by irreversible electrical-current
dissipation, summed over the complete divertor assembly.
items.documentation:
Current-driven ohmic-deposition power is the irreversible conversion of
electrical work into heat in divertor targets, attributable to electric
currents and their associated electric fields. It represents net power
deposited in the target assembly.

For target conducting domains indexed by $i$, the current-dissipation power
is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{div,ohm}} = \sum_i \int_{V_i} \mathbf{j}_i \cdot \mathbf{E}_i\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{div,ohm}}$ is the total divertor ohmic-deposition power,
$i$ indexes the divertor targets, $V_i$ is the conducting domain of target
$i$, $\mathbf{j}_i$ is its electric-current density, $\mathbf{E}_i$ is its
electric field, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the differential volume element. The
integrand is the local rate of irreversible electrical-work conversion into
heat.

The scope is the sum over all divertor targets, with no inner-target,
outer-target, or individual-target selection and no target-level breakdown.
This is the divertor-localized component of
[total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation](name:total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation),
whose broader aggregation covers the complete applicable conducting domain.

This mechanism-specific quantity excludes power attributed to radiative,
conductive, convective, neutral-particle, or recombination deposition
channels. Unlike
[deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current](name:deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current),
which isolates a halo-current contribution at one target, it aggregates the
accepted ohmic or current-driven contribution over the complete divertor
target assembly. It is also distinct from
[power_at_divertor_target](name:power_at_divertor_target), which denotes
power at one target without this all-target ohmic aggregation.

Sign convention: Positive when net electrical-current work deposits power
into the divertor targets.

items.name: electric_field
items.description:
Local vector electric field equal to the force per unit charge on a positive
stationary test charge, including electrostatic, inductive, and
electromagnetic-wave contributions.
items.documentation:
The electric field $\mathbf{E}$ is the local force per unit positive charge
on a stationary test charge. It is the complete vector quantity from which
projections such as the [vertical electric
field](name:vertical_electric_field) and field-parallel electric field are
formed.

In terms of electromagnetic potentials, the field is defined by

$$
\mathbf{E} = -\nabla\Phi - \frac{\partial\mathbf{A}}{\partial t}
$$

where $\Phi$ is the electrostatic potential, $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic
vector potential, and $t$ is time. The first term is electrostatic and the
second is inductive; their sum also describes wave fields, including the
[wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field). The electrostatic
contribution is related to the [electrostatic
potential](name:electrostatic_potential). Cylindrical projections use the
right-handed $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
increasing toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved cylindrical component points
toward increasing $R$, $\phi$, or $Z$, or when a field-parallel component
points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor
items.description:
Nuclear energy deposition rate integrated throughout the material volume of
one divertor structure, including neutron and other nuclear heating sources.
items.documentation:
Nuclear heating power of a divertor is the rate at which nuclear
interactions deposit energy throughout the material volume of that divertor
structure.

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{div}}} q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the nuclear heating power,
$q'''_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local volumetric nuclear
energy-deposition rate at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the
material volume of the divertor, and $dV$ is the differential volume
element.

The quantity applies to one indexed divertor structure and aggregates
neutron and all other included nuclear heating sources over its complete
material volume. It excludes energy deposited by nonnuclear convective
transport, such as [power of a divertor due to
convection](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection), and is distinct from
surface power deposited at an individual target, such as [neutral power at a
divertor target](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target).

items.name: poloidal_ion_state_particle_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective poloidal convection velocity for ion charge-state particle
transport, representing the signed pinch contribution rather than the ion
bulk flow.
items.documentation:
Effective poloidal convection velocity for ion charge-state particle
transport is the coefficient of the convective, or pinch, contribution to
transport of the particle density of a specified ion charge state. It is
distinct from the poloidal component of the ion bulk velocity.

The associated poloidal convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol,conv}} = n\,v_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol,conv}}$ is the poloidal component of convective
particle flux, $n$ is the particle density of the specified ion charge
state, and $v_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component of
ion_state_particle_convection_velocity. The projection is taken in the local
poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with
the poloidal direction defined by increasing poloidal angle. The
corresponding radial coefficient is
[radial_ion_state_particle_convection_velocity](name:radial_ion_state_particle_convection_velocity),
while
[poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity)
applies the same transport concept to neutral particles.

items.name: current_density
items.description:
Current density is the vector flux density of conventional electric charge,
equal to electric current per unit area normal to the flow. It points in the
direction of positive charge transport and includes all charged-particle
contributions unless a narrower current-density quantity is specified.
items.documentation:
Current density $\mathbf{J}$ is the vector density of conventional electric
charge flux at a point. It represents the signed flow of electric charge
carried by charged particles, with direction defined by positive charge
transport.

A kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the
particle distribution functions:

$$
\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes charged species,
$q_s$ is the species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_s$ is
the velocity-space distribution function. In quasistatic equilibrium it is
the source term in Ampere's law, $\nabla \times \mathbf{B} = \mu_0
\mathbf{J}$ when displacement current is neglected, and steady charge
conservation gives $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{J}=0$.

This quantity excludes displacement-current density and is distinct from a
scalar electric current, which is the flux of $\mathbf{J}$ through a
specified surface. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height, the geometric components are the projections along $(\hat{R},
\hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$: radial_current_density, toroidal_current_density, and
vertical_current_density. The full vector has direction rather than a single
scalar sign; scalar components and projections inherit the positive
direction of their defining basis vector or unit vector.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque vector transferred to thermal
ions in a selected charge state.
items.documentation:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque vector transferred to thermal
ions in a selected charge state is the net vector angular-momentum transfer
received by that thermal-ion population through Coulomb collisions. It
retains all spatial components of the collisional torque rather than only a
single projection.

It is defined as the volume integral of the local Coulomb-collisional torque
density transferred to the selected charge-state population:

$$
\boldsymbol{T}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi} = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi}(\boldsymbol{x})\, dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{T}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi}$ is this torque vector,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{i,\chi}$ is the local
Coulomb-collisional torque density transferred to thermal ions in charge
state $\chi$ of ion species $i$, $\boldsymbol{x}$ is position, $V$ is the
integrated plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

The scope is one thermal-ion species in one selected charge state within the
integrated plasma volume; as an extensive vector quantity, it is
volume-integrated and not averaged. It is charge-state-resolved, not summed
over charge states, and excludes electrons, neutrals, fast ions, external
momentum input, noncollisional electromagnetic torques, charge-exchange or
other atomic-process torques, transport-flux divergences, and wall or
boundary torques.

When resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height,
[`toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions`](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions)
is the $\phi$ projection of this vector. Only that toroidal projection
enters
[`total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions`](name:total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions);
the radial and vertical components of this vector are not included in that
scalar total. The charge-state-summed vector
[`thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions`](name:thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions)
is obtained by summing this vector over all charge states of the same
thermal-ion species.

Sign convention: Positive when a component resolved in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame points along $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or
$+\hat{Z}$, respectively; the toroidal projection is positive in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of boron, including neutral atoms and
all ionization states, evaluated on the plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the boron particle number density averaged over the last
closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary. It includes neutral
boron and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+, rather than
selecting a single charge state. It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart
of [boron density at the plasma
boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary).

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm B}\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm B}\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

Here $n_{\mathrm B}$ is the local total boron particle number density,
$\psi$ is the poloidal-flux surface label, $\psi_b$ identifies the
plasma-boundary surface, and $dS$ is its surface element. The result is an
average over the complete surface, not the density at a selected point or
for a selected ionization state.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux
items.description:
Parallel ion charge-state energy flux is the signed conductive and
convective energy transported along the local magnetic field per unit
perpendicular area and time for one ion species and charge state.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state energy flux is the net conductive and convective
energy transport along the local magnetic field, measured per unit area
perpendicular to that field and per unit time.

The field-aligned projection is defined by:

$$
