\Gamma_{\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel}$ is the signed parallel energy flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W}$ is the [ion charge-state energy-flux
vector](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) for the selected species and
charge state, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and $|\mathbf{B}|$
is its magnitude. The subscript $W$ identifies the energy transport channel.

This local quantity applies to one ion species in one specified charge
state, without summing over species or charge states. Its edge-plasma scope
includes the scrape-off layer and divertor. It excludes perpendicular energy
transport and is not restricted to the conductive contribution alone.

It is the parallel component of the parent energy flux, not its magnitude or
a surface-integrated power. Unlike the [parallel ion charge-state particle
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), it represents
transported energy rather than transported particle number.

Sign convention: Positive when net energy transport by the specified ion
charge state is in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Full physical extent of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its
first local tangential axis. This object-local axis is tangent to the mirror
surface and is the axis parameterized by the first local tangential
coordinate; the width applies to rectangular mirror geometry.
items.documentation:
Full physical extent of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its
first local tangential axis is the edge-to-edge span of the mirror surface
in that object-local tangential direction. The first local tangential axis
is the axis parameterized by the [first local tangential
coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).

For a rectangular mirror surface, let $u_1$ denote the first local
tangential coordinate on the mirror surface $\mathcal{M}$. The width is the
range of that coordinate over the mirror surface:

$$
w_1 = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{M}} u_1(\mathbf{x}) - \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{M}} u_1(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $w_1$ is the first local tangential width and $\mathbf{x}$ is a point
on the mirror surface.

This quantity applies to rectangular mirror geometry and is distinct from
both a coordinate value at a point and the [second local tangential
width](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
As a full extent rather than a signed displacement, it is unchanged by
reversing the positive sense of the first local tangential coordinate.

items.name: power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
Power quantity associated with a single breeder blanket module, abstracting
over incident neutron surface loads, volumetric nuclear energy deposition,
plasma radiation, and total thermal output as distinct energy-budget
components.
items.documentation:
A breeder blanket module participates in multiple distinct energy-exchange
pathways between the fusion plasma and the blanket structure. The principal
power channels resolved at the module level include the neutron surface load
characterized by
[incident_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:incident_neutron_power_of_breeder_blanket_module),
the volumetric nuclear energy deposited inside the module through scattering
and capture reactions described by neutron_power_of_breeder_blanket_module,
and the electromagnetic photon flux from plasma bremsstrahlung and line
radiation quantified by
[radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

The total power delivered to the module coolant combines these channels:

$$
P_\mathrm{module} = P_n + P_\mathrm{rad,abs} + P_\mathrm{aux}
$$

where $P_n$ is the deposited neutron power, $P_\mathrm{rad,abs}$ is the
absorbed fraction of incident plasma radiation after surface reflection, and
$P_\mathrm{aux}$ covers auxiliary heating contributions; nuclear
multiplication reactions in the tritium-breeding material can amplify $P_n$
above the incident neutron surface load.

Module-level power quantities are computed from neutronics transport
simulations for nuclear deposition channels, coupled with plasma radiation
models for photon loads, and validated against calorimetric measurements of
coolant enthalpy rise, the latter captured by
[net_thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:net_thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).
The blanket-wide integral summed over all modules is given by
[nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket).

items.name: wave_voltage
items.description:
Wave voltage is the electrical potential-difference signal associated with a
detected electromagnetic probing wave returned after interaction with a
plasma cutoff layer. It is the generic wave-related voltage quantity; child
names specify scalar forms such as amplitude.
items.documentation:
Wave voltage is the electrical potential-difference signal associated with a
detected electromagnetic probing wave returned after interaction with a
plasma cutoff layer. It denotes the wave-related voltage quantity
generically, without restricting it to a particular scalar form such as
amplitude.

As a voltage, the underlying signed signal is a potential difference:

$$
V_\mathrm{wave}(t) = \Phi_\mathrm{sig}(t) - \Phi_\mathrm{ref}(t)
$$

where $V_\mathrm{wave}$ is the wave-voltage signal, $\Phi_\mathrm{sig}$ is
the electric potential at the signal terminal of the receiving circuit,
$\Phi_\mathrm{ref}$ is the electric potential at its reference terminal, and
$t$ is time.

The scope is limited to voltage quantities representing the received probing
wave after plasma cutoff-layer interaction. It excludes source or launcher
drive voltage, voltages unrelated to the returned probing wave, and
non-voltage wave quantities such as electric field, phase, or frequency.

Child names specify the scalar form or reduction of this parent quantity.
The [wave-voltage amplitude](name:wave_voltage_amplitude) is the amplitude
of the same detected wave-voltage signal, not a separate kind of wave
signal; the parent itself does not impose an amplitude, envelope, or
root-mean-square convention unless a child qualifier states one.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric potential at the signal terminal
of the receiving circuit is greater than the electric potential at its
reference terminal.

items.name: perpendicular_wave_vector_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description:
Non-negative magnitude of the RF wave-vector component perpendicular to the
local equilibrium magnetic field launched by an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna.
items.documentation:
This quantity measures the transverse spatial variation of the
radio-frequency wave launched by an ion-cyclotron heating antenna, relative
to the local equilibrium magnetic field.

The perpendicular wave-vector magnitude is defined by

$$
k_\perp = \left|\mathbf{k} - (\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}})\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right|
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the local RF wave vector,
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and vertical bars denote
vector magnitude.

Only the component transverse to the magnetic field is included; the
parallel component is excluded. The result is non-negative and has no
propagation-direction sign. It is the antenna-specific counterpart of the
general perpendicular wave-vector magnitude.

items.name: energy_confinement_enhancement_factor
items.description:
Dimensionless ratio comparing the plasma energy confinement time with the
IPB98(y,2) reference scaling prediction.
items.documentation:
The energy confinement enhancement factor is the multiplicative departure of
a plasma’s global energy confinement time from the IPB98(y,2) reference
scaling prediction. It indicates whether energy is retained longer or
shorter than the reference predicts for the corresponding scaling inputs.

The factor is defined by:

$$
h_{98} = \frac{\tau_E}{\tau_{E,\mathrm{IPB98(y,2)}}}
$$

where $h_{98}$ is the energy confinement enhancement factor, $\tau_E$ is the
plasma energy confinement time, and $\tau_{E,\mathrm{IPB98(y,2)}}$ is the
energy confinement time predicted by the IPB98(y,2) reference scaling.

This is a global plasma quantity: the numerator represents the confinement
of the total stored plasma energy relative to the corresponding net
energy-loss power, aggregated over the plasma rather than assigned to a
local region or individual transport channel. It is not itself an energy
confinement time, stored energy, power, or local transport coefficient.

A value of one denotes agreement with the reference scaling; a value greater
than one denotes longer confinement, and a value less than one denotes
shorter confinement than the reference prediction.
